checks: For a common closed halfspace the average of two endpoint cap points belongs to the same halfspace and to the full Minkowski midpoint. The positive endpoint volume makes the averaged cap body full-dimensional.

The volume-root assumption and Brunn–Minkowski give equal positive volumes at both ends of the compact convex inclusion chain. Strict separation of a point outside the smaller set, then interpolation toward an interior point, gives a positive-volume difference whenever containment is strict.

The assumed cover unions the cap equalities into K⊆(A+B)/2. If the planes pass through a common point and normals have a positive dependence, their positively weighted margins sum to zero at each point, which gives the cover.

overlap.comparison: It has the same cap-set equality step for one actual mixed depth-attaining cap with distinct endpoint thresholds and added equal-mass conclusions. The frozen theorem uses arbitrary common cap covers and no depth or stationarity premise.

Its similar union step occurs only after equality of the optimized raw ordinary-depth roots and selection of active caps through three different optimal marks. The supplied cap cover here is independent of those optimizers.

readability: The cap cover need only cover K. It need not cover the entire space unless obtained from the positive-dependence sufficient condition.
